subject: general
question: Eight times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 46 years. After 10 years, three times Q’s age will be 12 years less than eight times P’s age at that time. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **P** and **Q** be their present ages.

From first condition: 8P − Q = 46 ⇒ 8P = Q + 46

From second condition: 3(Q + 10) = 8(P + 10) − 12

Substitute 8P with (Q + 46): 3Q + 30 = (Q + 46) + 80 − 12

2Q = 114 − 30 ⇒ 2Q = 84 ⇒ Q = 42

**∴ The correct answer is 42 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Relation between **P** and **Q** at present and after **10 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f529a0074d79aae8a0d942258473ba0f961b7c0a41992ce5b6e95e4110657799.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 8P − Q = 46 --- (i)

⇒ 3(Q + 10) = 8(P + 10) − 12

⇒ 3Q + 30 = 8P + 80 − 12

⇒ 3Q + 30 = 8P + 68

⇒ 8P − 3Q = −38 --- (ii)

Subtract (ii) from (i):

⇒ (8P − Q) − (8P − 3Q) = 46 − (−38)

⇒ 8P − Q − 8P + 3Q = 46 + 38

⇒ 2Q = 84

⇒ Q = 42

**∴ The correct answer is 42 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

A system of equations like a₁x + b₁y = c₁ can be solved using **substitution** or **elimination** methods.

Age Problems Logic

If the current age is x, then age after 'n' years is **(x + n)** and age 'n' years ago was **(x − n)**.

Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** regardless of the number of years passed.</p
